clue.text: Unfashionable women's wear with fringes?

parts.note: something unfashionable is out, no longer in style
skirts are garments worn by women

explanation.surface: A remark that women's clothing with tassels and fringes has gone out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringes' looks like decoration on the skirts, but it is the definition: the outer edges of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: The fringes of a town are its outlying edge districts, a synonym.

clue.text: "Piscine" means slightly aloof

explanation.surface: A pedantic remark that the word for fishlike also describes someone a little standoffish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Piscine' as the phrase OF FISH, since piscine means relating to fish; run together it gives the word for cool and distant.
explanation.definitionFit: Piscine means pertaining to fish; someone slightly aloof is cool, standoffish and unfriendly in manner.

clue.text: It'll rot a poorly cooked pancake!

indicators.note: food poorly cooked is messed up, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a badly made flatbread will spoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly cooked' rearranges the letters of IT'LL ROT, giving TORTILL; the apostrophe adds no letter, and A ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican flat round of unleavened bread is loosely described as a kind of thin pancake.

clue.text: Knockout, unfortunately, for some animals

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout
alas is an exclamation meaning sadly, unfortunately

explanation.surface: A boxing knockout that sadly involves some animals.
explanation.definitionFit: These Australian tree-dwelling marsupials are examples of animals.

clue.text: Free Germany, and the French puzzle!

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear of something
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
le is French for the (masculine)

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to liberate Germany, followed by a puzzling reference to France.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle in the form of a question with a trick answer is a conundrum, a synonym.

clue.text: Point frequently and observe this weakness

parts.note: S, south, is one of the compass points
oft is an old word for often, frequently
to spot something is to observe or notice it

explanation.surface: Advice to point often and notice where something is weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point here, not a verb; 'this' just leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fondness or affection that one cannot resist is a weakness for something.

clue.text: Spoil the church parade

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage

explanation.surface: Someone ruins the church procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a procession, as in a protest walk or military procession.

clue.text: Attractive sort of curtains found in sorcery

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside another here

parts.note: magic is sorcery, the casting of spells
net curtains are a light sheer kind of curtain

explanation.surface: A charming type of curtain discovered amid witchcraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' signals a container. Net curtains are thin see-through curtains common in British windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive in the physical sense of drawing iron to it, or figuratively alluring.

clue.text: Terrible decay — not even in the end!

parts.note: rot is decay or decomposition

indicators.note: not even means the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are kept from these words

explanation.surface: A lament about awful decay that refuses to come out even at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not even' takes the odd letters of THE END: T, E, N; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten in its informal sense of awful or very bad, synonymous with dreadful.

clue.text: A book that's difficult to support

parts.note: hard means difficult
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A volume that is a struggle to endorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A book bound in stiff covers, as opposed to a paperback, is an example of a book.

clue.text: Footballer supporting a place for hospital beds

parts.note: if you are for something you are supporting it
a ward is a room of beds in a hospital

explanation.surface: A football player backing a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: A striker or attacking player in football is called by this positional name.

clue.text: Noted date had switched and set off

indicators.note: letters that had switched have changed places, so this fodder is reordered

explanation.surface: A memorable appointment was swapped and then got going.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to explode it, synonymous with exploded.

clue.text: Sacred view from Rome?

parts.note: holy means sacred
to see is to view

explanation.surface: A question about a religious outlook emanating from the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's seat; the Pope's see in Rome is the government of the Catholic Church, so the whole clue also hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal jurisdiction based in Vatican City in Rome, the central government of the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Darling, a French one has a flower!

parts.note: a pet is a darling, a favourite
un is French for a
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An affectionate claim that one French person owns a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plant with trumpet-shaped blooms, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Brazil could be difficult to beat

definitions.text: Brazil could be difficult to beat

parts.words: Brazil could be difficult to beat
parts.note: reads like praise of the Brazilian football team, but a Brazil is a tough-shelled nut, and the idiom means a problem or person hard to overcome

explanation.surface: A pundit warns that the Brazilian football team will be tough to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a tough problem or person not easily overcome, and a Brazil nut is notoriously tough-shelled.

clue.text: Taking into account everything due

parts.note: all means everything
money owing is due, not yet paid

explanation.surface: Considering that the whole sum is outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowing for something means making provision for it, considering it.

clue.text: Could one hold up entrance?

parts.note: hold up suggests a robbery at the door, but it means physically supporting the frame of a doorway

explanation.surface: Asking whether a robber could hold up a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright timber at each side of a door frame bears the frame's weight.

clue.text: Inconvenient dawn tour was organised

indicators.note: something organised is arranged afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An awkward sunrise excursion had been arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unfortunate or awkward, unexpected and unwelcome.

clue.text: Unsuccessful, and a bit over adapted

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so these letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A failure, and a little altered in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' is the anagram signal, making BORTIVE after the A; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abortive means failing to achieve its purpose, fruitless.

clue.text: Look — beer has failed to gain an advantage!

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
stout is a dark strong beer

explanation.surface: Someone points out that the beer missed out on a winning edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss out on a benefit or be beaten is the phrasal verb meaning failed to profit.

clue.text: Thus delicate material provides comfort

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
lace is a delicate open-work fabric

explanation.surface: Therefore a fine fabric brings consolation.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation in distress, a synonym.

clue.text: Think of taking drink with model

parts.note: to sup is to take drink in small mouthfuls
to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: Considering having a drink with a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to imagine or assume, as in picturing a hypothetical.

clue.text: Father points to warnings

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a male parent
N and S, north and south, are compass points

explanation.surface: Dad gestures towards the alerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirens are loud alarm signals on police cars, ambulances and air-raid systems.

clue.text: Best get up before one, working for a drink

indicators.note: get up in a down clue means the word for best is turned upward, read bottom to top

parts.note: top means best, foremost
the Roman numeral I is one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: The winner rises ahead of another and works up a thirst.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'get up' reverses the word upward; 'before' only says it comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A potion is a liquid dose, medicinal or magical, so a kind of drink.

clue.text: My previous wife? Saucy and skilled!

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
pert means saucy, cheeky

explanation.surface: Someone describes a former spouse as cheeky and capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Expert means highly skilled and knowledgeable.

clue.text: Women, sick, might have resolution

parts.note: ill means sick
might is power, strength

explanation.surface: Women who are unwell might still show determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution in the sense of determination and self-control is a synonym.

clue.text: Journalist provided with cold building

parts.note: ED, editor, is a journalist
if means provided that
ice is cold, frozen water

explanation.surface: A reporter is supplied with a chilly office.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large imposing building, a synonym.

clue.text: Speculated loudly whether one had an invitation

indicators.note: loudly means the word for speculated is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: guessed means speculated

explanation.surface: Someone wondered aloud whether they had been invited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' signals a sound-alike: the past tense of guess sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person invited to a party or event is the one who received the invite.

clue.text: Cid finest managed to sterilise

indicators.note: managed suggests letters handled and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: El Cid, best of knights, contrived to sanitise things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges CID FINEST. El Cid was a medieval Spanish hero.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinfect is to clean of germs, synonymous with sterilise.
